newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli finance minister to report on budget.
newsitem.headline: Israeli finance minister to report on budget.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor will report to ministers on the state of the 1997 budget at the next cabinet meeting on February 21, the Treasury said on Tuesday.
The budget deficit reached 1.28 billion shekels in January, well above the targeted level. The government usually runs a budget surplus in January.

"Meridor told the prime minister (Benjamin Netanyahu) that he intended to report to the cabinet about the state of the 1997 bduget based on the January figures and on expected developments both on the revenue and expenditure side," the Treasury said.

Meridor told the parliamentary finance committee on Tuesday that spending would only be subject to a quarterly review. In its statement on Tuesday the Treasury echoed that view, despite Meridor's plans to raise the issue just six weeks into the fiscal year.
"Meridor believes that there have to be set dates for doing this kind of review once a quarter," the Treasury said.

On Sunday, Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel expresssed deep concern about the January deficit and called for frequent spending reviews. He indicated that interest rates would not fall sharply in real terms unless the deficit was on target.
The 1997 budget calls for a deficit equal to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product. Last year, the deficit grew to 4.7 percent of GDP, nearly double the planned figure.
The Treasury said the January deficit was due to a one-off payment to the healthcare network.

"The Treasury notes that one cannot learn from the figures of a single month, but if it becomes clear that the budget is deviating from its planned course the necessary steps will be taken immediately," the ministry said.
